label: Is my baby too young?
reassure: There's no single 'right' age. What matters is what suits your baby and the kind of trip you have in mind. Start with what fits their age now.

links.label: Is baby ready? Age by age

label: Crying on the plane or train
reassure: Babies cry, and crew and fellow passengers have seen it many times. Having a few things to try, in order, makes it feel much more manageable.

label: Messing up their sleep
reassure: A few wobbly nights away from home are normal, not a sign you got it wrong. Protecting the important naps and keeping bedtime familiar helps.

links.label: Line up naps with the journey

label: Forgetting something important
reassure: Most things can be bought where you're going. The few that can't, like documents and medicines, are at the top of your list.

label: Feeding on the go
reassure: Breast, bottle or snacks: a little planning about when and where the feeds will happen makes them calmer, and you don't need to be perfect.

links.label: See where feeds fall on travel day
Ask the airline about milk and baby food

label: Baby getting ill away from home
reassure: It's one of the most common worries. Insurance that covers baby, a small health kit and a chat with your GP or health visitor before you go all help you feel ready.

links.label: Medicines for you and your child

label: Being judged by strangers
reassure: Most people are kinder than the stares suggest. Your job is your baby, not the audience. You're doing better than you think.

links.label: What to do in the moment

label: Booking the wrong thing
reassure: You don't need to know every rule, just the right questions. Ask before you pay and get the answers in writing.

links.label: Questions to ask before you book
